en: Udāna 7.6 Taṇhāsaṅkhayasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now on that occasion the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña was sitting not far from the Blessed One, having folded his legs crosswise and set his body erect, reflecting upon liberation through the destruction of craving.
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise and set his body erect, reflecting upon liberation through the destruction of craving.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For one whose root is not in the earth,
where would there be leaves or creepers?”
Who could possibly blame that wise one who is freed from bonds?
